# Didache Chapter 14 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Hierosolymitanus (H), Didache 14 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/DID_014_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 14

**1** And on the Lord's day of the Lord, being gathered together, break bread and give thanks, having confessed your transgressions beforehand, so that your sacrifice may be pure.

**2** But let anyone who has a dispute with his fellow not come together with you until they have been reconciled, so that your sacrifice may not be defiled.

**3** For this is what was said by the Lord: "In every place and time, offer me a pure sacrifice; for I am a great king, says the Lord, and my name is wonderful among the nations."

---

*EMET notes: V.1 — "Lord's day of the Lord" (κατὰ κυριακὴν δὲ κυρίου) — the Greek is redundant, combining κυριακήν (the Lord's, an adjective) with κυρίου (of the Lord, a genitive). This may be emphatic: "the Lord's own day of the Lord." This is the earliest non-New Testament reference to Sunday as a distinct Christian assembly day (cf. Rev 1:10). "Break bread" = the Eucharist (cf. Acts 2:42; 20:7). V.3 — quotes Malachi 1:11, 14 (LXX, with modification). In its original context, Malachi speaks of a future universal sacrifice. The Didache applies it to the Christian eucharist as the fulfillment of Malachi's prophecy — a remarkable early use of fulfilled prophecy for eucharistic theology.*
